extracted.intended_audience: legislators, congressional staff, agency counsel, administrative law practitioners, and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Senate floor text and enacted amendment to Section 3 of the Administrative Procedure Act (1946) setting publication, disclosure, exemption, indexing, and judicial-remedy rules for agency records, opinions, and procedures. Includes floor debate proposing clarifications and examples (e.g., wage data, investigatory files, intra-agency memoranda).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the Federal Register (what to publish)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent involved in national-security secrecy or internal management matters, every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register for the guidance of the public (A) descriptions of its central and field organization and the established places at which, the officers from whom, and methods whereby, the public may secure information, make submittals or requests, or obtain decisions; (B) statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined, including the nature and requirements of all formal or informal procedures available, rules of procedure, descriptions of forms available or the places at which forms may be obtained, and instructions as to the scope and contents of all papers, reports, or examinations; (C) substantive rules of general applicability adopted as authorized by law and statements of general policy or interpretations of general applicability formulated and adopted by the agency and (D) every amendment, revision, or repeal of the foregoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpublished matters required to be in the Federal Register cannot bind or adversely affect persons who lack actual notice. Exceptions limited to (1) functions requiring secrecy for national security/foreign policy and (2) matters relating solely to internal management of an agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of agency opinions, orders, rules, statements, and interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent covered by Executive order secrecy (national defense/foreign policy), internal personnel rules/practices, or specific statutory exemptions, every agency shall make available for public inspection and copying all final opinions (including concurring and dissenting opinions) and all orders made in adjudication of cases, and those rules, statements of policy, and interpretations which have been adopted by the agency, affect the public and are not required to be published in the Federal Register, unless such materials are promptly published and copies offered for sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publish or make available final adjudicative opinions and non-FR rules/policies that affect the public; deletions of identifying details are allowed to prevent clearly unwarranted invasions of personal privacy or to protect the public interest, but written justification for deletions is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing requirement for final orders/opinions/rules/policies/interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall maintain and make available for public inspection and copying a current index providing identifying information for the public as to each final order, opinion, rule, statement of policy, and interpretation of general applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An index must be current and publicly available so parties can find controlling agency materials. The statute also ties citation/precedent status to indexing/publication or prior actual notice (see citation limitation entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation/precedent limitation for post-effective agency materials
rubrics_metrics.description: No final order or opinion may be cited as precedent, and no opinion, rule, statement of policy, or interpretation issued, adopted, or promulgated after the effective date of this Act may be relied upon, used, or cited as precedent by an agency against any private party unless it has been indexed and either made available or published as provided or unless prior to the commencement of the proceeding all private parties shall have actual notice of the terms thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents agencies from surprising private parties with unpublished policies; ensures notice-first principle for adverse enforcement or reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: General obligation to make agency records promptly available
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall, in accordance with published rules stating time, place, and procedure, make all its records promptly available to any person except those records or parts thereof falling within specified exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a presumption of disclosure with enumerated exceptions; agencies must publish rules describing access procedures and expedite handling of complaints in court (see judicial remedies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — functions requiring secrecy for national security or foreign policy (Exec order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records 'specifically required by Executive order to be kept secret for the protection of the national defense or foreign policy' are exempt from disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classic national-security/foreign-policy exemption tied to Executive orders; remains an exception to publication and disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — internal personnel rules and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Records that 'relate solely to the internal personnel rules and practices of any agency' are exempt from public inspection and copying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects purely internal procedures; does not cover substantive rules or policies affecting the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — specific statutory exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Records that are 'specifically exempted from disclosure by statute' are not subject to the disclosure requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where another statute explicitly exempts disclosure, that statutory exemption controls; agencies should cite the specific statutory basis when withholding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — trade secrets and information obtained from the public and customarily privileged or confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade secrets and other information obtained from the public and customarily privileged or confidential are exempt from disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Floor debate raised concern that the phrase might not cover data 'obtained in confidence' (e.g., wage data submitted to Bureau of Labor Statistics) and suggested adding 'in confidence' to protect such inputs; opponents worried adding 'in confidence' could broaden agency ability to claim confidentiality. Agencies should consider whether information is customarily treated as confidential and whether disclosure would harm data sources or enforcement functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — intra-agency or interagency memoranda or letters dealing solely with matters of law or policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Intra-agency or interagency memoranda or letters dealing solely with matters of law or policy are exempt from disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute (as enacted) limits the exemption to memoranda 'dealing solely with matters of law or policy.' Floor debate noted concerns that excluding 'matters of fact' could force disclosure of factual evaluations (e.g., credibility assessments) and chill candid internal judgments; drafters argued work-product and other privileges would still protect certain materials if facts themselves are otherwise unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — personnel files, medical files, and similar matters implicating privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel files, medical files, and similar matter the disclosure of which would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy-based exemption framed by 'clearly unwarranted invasion' standard; agencies may redact identifying details from otherwise disclosable opinions/orders to prevent privacy invasions but must provide written justification for deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — investigatory files compiled for law enforcement purposes (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigatory files compiled for law enforcement purposes are exempt except to the extent they are by law available to a private party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senate debate explored alternative formulations (including explicit alignment with Jencks rule and proposals to protect witness statements until testimony). The enacted language adopts a limitation—investigatory law-enforcement files are generally exempt unless law already provides access to a private party; proponents argued this prevents fishing expeditions and protects investigatory effectiveness, while opponents worried about excessive secrecy. Agencies should interpret this in light of existing case law and any statutes providing party access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — examination, operating, or condition reports for financial institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Records contained in or related to examination, operating, or condition reports prepared by, on behalf of, or for the use of any agency responsible for the regulation or supervision of financial institutions are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects supervisory reports for banks and similar institutions to preserve supervisory confidentiality and financial stability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial remedies and standards of review for unlawful withholding
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon complaint, a U.S. district court in the complainant's district or where the agency is situated shall have jurisdiction to enjoin the agency from further withholding and to order production of improperly withheld records; the court shall determine the matter de novo, the burden is upon the agency to sustain its action by a preponderance of the evidence, the court may assess costs and reasonable attorneys' fees against the agency, and may punish responsible officers for contempt for noncompliance; proceedings authorized by this subsection shall be expedited and take precedence on the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes an affirmative private right of action with de novo review and a relatively demanding burden on the agency (preponderance), plus fee-shifting and contempt remedies; courts are instructed to expedite such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency recordkeeping of final votes
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency having more than one member shall keep a record of the final votes of each member in every agency proceeding and, except to the extent required to protect the national defense or foreign policy, such record shall be available for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency of collegial agency decisionmaking unless national security/foreign-policy secrecy applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on authority to withhold information
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section authorizes withholding of information or limiting the availability of records to the public except as specifically stated in this section, nor shall this section be authority to withhold information from Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constrains agencies to the enumerated exemptions only and preserves congressional access to agency information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'private party' for purposes of the section
rubrics_metrics.description: As used in this section, 'private party' means any party other than an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who benefits from the notice and anti-surprise protections and who may sue for improper withholding (private parties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of the amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: This amendment shall become effective one year following the date of the enactment of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a uniform delayed effective date to allow agencies to comply with new publication, indexing, and procedural obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written justification required for deletions/redactions
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent required to prevent a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy, an agency may delete identifying details when it makes available or publishes an opinion or order; and to the extent required to protect the public interest, an agency may delete identifying details when it makes available or publishes a rule, statement of policy, or interpretation; however, in any case the justification for the deletion must be fully explained in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document the reason for redaction in writing, providing an accountability trail and allowing review of whether the deletion was warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floor-proposed clarifications and examples (debate guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senators proposed clarifications to clauses: (1) strike 'prior to the commencement of the proceedings' (rejected by committee chairman as protective of private parties); (2) amend clause (4) to read 'trade secrets and information obtained from the public in confidence or customarily privileged or confidential' to protect wage data sources; (3) amend clause (5) to include 'matters of fact' so intra-agency memoranda dealing with facts might be exempt; (4) amend investigatory-files clause to protect witness statements until called and to reflect Jencks-like protections. The chairman offered substitute language: 'investigatory files compiled for law enforcement purposes except to the extent they are by law available to a private party.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These debate items illustrate potential ambiguities in the statutory text and the policy tradeoffs (protecting sources and candid internal deliberations vs. public access). They serve as interpretive cues and examples of how particular uses (e.g., Bureau of Labor Statistics wage surveys, NLRB investigations, witness statements) might be treated. Agencies and courts should consider these floor statements when construing ambiguous exemptions.
